Emma — really appreciate the clear ask and the SOW. Short answers up front so you can share with procurement:

- Yes, we can stack the SeedSprint promoter voucher with the standard onboarding credit for pilots in most cases.
- We can earmark up to USD 10k of onboarding credit as a conversion credit toward a future Dedicated commit, but the credit must be applied as an offset on the first 3 months of the Dedicated contract (cannot be cashed out).
- Promo vouchers (third-party/promoter) typically expire 12 months from issuance; our onboarding credit for active pilots is valid for 9 months from activation. Neither is refundable in cash, but both can be reallocated within the same legal entity with approvals.

Ben (AE) / Naomi (Finance) — can you confirm there are no unusual billing constraints for SeedSprint (they’re US-based, non-profit-ish cohort companies) and whether we can include the earmark language in the quote/DocuSign? I’ve attached the SOW Emma sent.

Next step: Emma — if procurement confirms Tue AM PT works, I’ll schedule a quick 20-min call to lock language and run a sample 3-month billing preview.

Thanks,
Irene Choi

Irene / Naomi — looping on this before we send formal language. My read: approve stacking and allow a USD 10k earmark for conversion, but we should add the following guardrails to the quote and SOW: 

- Earmarked credits apply only if a Dedicated contract is signed within 180 days of pilot activation.
- Earmark reduces the first three monthly invoices for Dedicated by equal installments (e.g., USD 3,333/mo).
- If the customer signs on as a different legal entity (e.g., startup spins out), credits are not transferable without a formal assignment and approval from Finance.
- No refunds. If the org terminates the pilot early, unused onboarding credits revert to Redwood.
